bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday appealed to financially well-off people and income tax payers to voluntarily give up the benefit of 125 units of free electricity and support the state's development. Also Read 5paisa Capital Wins Major Relief in Income Tax Appeal, Disallowance Cut to Rs 2.87 Crore Speaking at the two-day 'Pataliputra National Youth Parliament 2.0' event, Choudhary said the state government spends around Rs 23,000 crore every year on electricity subsidies. He said the government provides 125 units of free electricity to consumers across all income groups and urged those who can afford to pay their bills to give up the benefit. Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari , MP Shambhavi Choudhary and Youth Parliament founder Sayan Kunal were among those present at the event . The Chief Minister also highlighted the important role of young people in strengthening democracy and building a developed India. He said Bihar has a rich history of democratic values and that the youth must take responsibility for protecting and promoting them. Recalling India's freedom struggle, Choudhary said the country became independent in 1947 because of the sacrifices of freedom fighters. As India moves towards completing 80 years of Independence, he said people must renew their commitment to democratic values. He also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making India a developed nation by 2047 and said former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar had made important contributions to the state's development. Referring to the 1974 movement, Choudhary said young people had played a major role in bringing change . He added that today's generations, including Gen Z and Gen Alpha, must also come forward to strengthen democracy. He also called for organising the Youth Parliament every year to help young people understand democratic processes, constitutional values and their role in nation-building.

The chief minister made the appeal while addressing the Pataliputra National Youth Parliament-2.0 in Patna on Sunday. He said the Bihar government spends around Rs 23,000 crore every year on electricity subsidies, with the annual subsidy amount ranging between Rs 8,000 and Rs 10,000 per household. He said financially comfortable households, particularly income-tax payers, should consider giving up the subsidy and contributing towards Bihar's growth. In a statement, the BJP said Nabin will lead the ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ padyatra in Bihar and West Bengal on Monday against the Opposition’s “lies and anarchy”. “Bharatiya Janata Party national president Nitin Nabin will lead two major ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao Padyatras’ in Bihar and West Bengal on Monday as part of the party’s nationwide campaign against the Opposition’s misinformation, disinformation and organised anarchy,” it said. The BJP said the party’s campaign is a “movement against the lies, deception, conspiracies and anarchy being spread by a desperate and disillusioned Opposition.” “With the resolve of ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’, every BJP karyakarta is reaching out to villages and households to expose the Opposition’s false and fabricated narrative and apprise the people of the truth,” it added. bihar_raw_news.content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, while reviewing the progress of Mukhyamantri Registry Yojana at CM House, said that all ministers, MPs and MLAs should visit their ancestral villages on Dhateras or any village of their choice and personally oversee the completion of 100% property registrations under the scheme. He said that along with owning a plot or house, it is equally important to have valid and permanent revenue documents for the property. These documents establish the owner's legal rights and enable them to buy and sell their property. He directed departmental officials to implement the scheme as a large-scale campaign and ensure that all eligible property owners in the state receive free permanent registration of their land titles at the earliest. The campaign to provide permanent property registration would continue in the coming years as well. Next year, it would also be linked with the 'Year of Youth'. Over 12.87 lakh registrations completed Principal secretary, revenue, E Ramesh Kumar, informed at the meeting that, as of Nov 1, 2026, a total of 12,87,252 properties were registered across the state. Efforts are underway to complete 20 lakh registrations by November 15. MSME minister Chetanya Kashyap, minister of state Narendra Shivaji Patel, chief secretary Ashok Barnwal, additional chief secretary Neeraj Mandloi, secretary and commissioner, public relations, Manish Singh were also present. national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah directs to establish FRROs in all states by 2027 to promote India as attractive dest...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has directed the establishment of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) in all state capitals by next year. Currently, FRRO offices have been established in twenty States. The Home Ministry said that there has been a substantial increase in the number of foreigners visiting India for tourism, medical and education purposes and there is a need to appoint FRROs in all states. The Ministry said, this will ensure service accessibility, enhance regulatory compliance and promote India as an attractive destination. It said, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government is strengthening the institutional framework for management of foreign nationals through expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices. The Ministry informed that Central government is pursuing the matter of establishing FRRO’s in remaining States namely Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya. This will help foreigners visiting India obtain various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with State authorities and facilitate legitimate foreign visitors. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful stay of foreign nationals visiting or residing in India. It administers post-arrival registration for eligible categories of foreigners and issues a Registration Certificate or Residential Permit upon registration.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, it is a matter of pride for 140 crore Indians that the country has so far managed global challenges ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to the West Asia crisis effectively and sustained high growth. Addressing the gathering after inaugurating four-day Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, the Prime Minister said the global economy has witnessed unprecedented crises over the past few years and the West Asia crisis is still continuing. He said that this global crisis has sent a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. He said, the future of energy security lies in clean energy. Prime Minister Modi said, today, more than 50 per cent of India’s installed power capacity is based on non-fossil fuel sources. He said, India is firmly working towards achieving the target of 500 GigaWatt. Mr Modi highlighted that fossil fuel reserves are limited, while the potential of renewable energy is unlimited, and every region and country can benefit from it. Prime Minister Modi said, India is among the top three countries in solar and renewable energy sector. He added that this new phase of the solar revolution is not just about adoption but also depends on innovation. Mr Modi highlighted that in the last 12 years, more than 44 thousand government buildings have been connected to solar energy, resulting in savings of about seven hundred crore rupees annually. The Prime Minister stressed on the need to connect every government building, school, college, hospital, street-lighting system to solar energy. Prime Minister Modi said that farmers across the country are also benefiting from the PM-KUSUM scheme. He said, through this initiative, more than 30 lakh farmers have been provided with solar-powered irrigation facilities. Mr. Modi stated that estimates indicate that farmers can save approximately one lakh rupees annually by using solar-powered pumps. On the occasion, New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said that the renewable energy sector has attracted investments worth 67 billion dollars during the past two years. He said, under the guidance of Prime Minister Modi, India’s non-fossil fuel-based installed capacity has crossed 310 gigawatts, compared to 200 gigawatts in September 2024. Mr Joshi added that Foreign Direct Investment in the sector has also reached 6.2 billion dollars, reflecting strong investor confidence in the sector. The summit has been being organised by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy with the theme of Invest. Innovate. Inspire. Participants from more than 130 countries, including over 40 ministers, are attending the summit. It has brought together policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders to promote clean energy investments, technological innovation and international partnerships. In this summit, Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom is participating as country partners. Thirteen States and Union Territories are showcasing their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.

China and Bangladesh, being out of the semi-final race, will play for the 5th position. Today, India will take on South Korea, China will play with Bangladesh and Japan will face Malaysia. ANI | Updated: 02-11-2026 10:48 IST | Created: 02-11-2026 10:48 IST India, EU discuss FTA implementation, customs cooperation and market access in Brussels. (Photo-PIB). Image Credit: ANI SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... India and the European Union (EU) have discussed preparations for implementing their Free Trade Agreement (FTA), along with measures to improve market access, simplify customs procedures and strengthen supply chain cooperation during high-level meetings in Brussels. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held meetings with senior European Commission officials, including Ditte Juul Jørgensen, Director-General of the Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security (DG TRADE); Koen Doens, Director-General of the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA); and Gerassimos Thomas, Director-General of the Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union (DG TAXUD). According to an official statement by the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry, during his meeting with Jørgensen, both sides discussed ways to facilitate two-way trade, improve market access, strengthen supply chain resilience and create new business opportunities for companies in India and the EU. They reaffirmed their commitment to a fair, balanced and mutually beneficial agreement and agreed to maintain close engagement to address the remaining procedural and implementation-related issues. In a separate meeting with Thomas, discussions focused on customs cooperation, trade facilitation and preparations for implementing the India-EU FTA. Both sides highlighted the importance of efficient, transparent and digitally enabled customs procedures to reduce transaction costs for businesses and ensure the smooth movement of goods. The meetings come after India and the European Union officially concluded negotiations on the FTA at the 16th India-EU Summit on January 27, 2026, in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The agreement is currently undergoing legal scrubbing and verification ahead of its proposed signing in mid-December 2026. Its full ratification and entry into force are targeted for mid-2027. The agreement is expected to provide wider market access for businesses on both sides. Under the proposed arrangement, tariffs will be eliminated on over 99 per cent of Indian exports to the EU, benefiting labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, leather and jewellery. India will also reduce duties on over 96 per cent of European goods, including a phased reduction in automobile tariffs to 10 per cent under an annual quota of 250,000 units. Apart from trade negotiations, Agrawal also met representatives of the diamond industry associated with the Antwerp diamond ecosystem. Discussions covered the global diamond value chain, certification and traceability...
